S1.headline: The pod checks the spot
S1.cite: c1 c2 c11 c17 c19 c31 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S1.body: Zipline wants FAA approval to fly delivery drones over Houston, San Antonio, Austin, Amarillo and El Paso. The FAA takes comment until October 11th.
strings: Zipline wants FAA approval to fly delivery drones over Houston, San Antonio, Austin, Amarillo and El Paso. The FAA takes comment until October 11th.

S2.headline: It holds at 330 feet
S2.cite: c11 c17 c19 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S2.body: The pod goes down on a line and back up while the aircraft hovers, for about 75 seconds. The aircraft, the pod and the line are drawn larger than they are.
strings: The pod goes down on a line and back up while the aircraft hovers, for about 75 seconds. The aircraft, the pod and the line are drawn larger than they are.
c11 c17 c19 TEXAS AI DOCKET

S3.headline: It judges the yard
S3.body: On the way down the pod steers itself sideways and evaluates the spot. If the spot is clear, it keeps descending.
strings: On the way down the pod steers itself sideways and evaluates the spot. If the spot is clear, it keeps descending.

S4.headline: When it can't tell
S4.body: If the pod can't identify the target and judge it, the draft says an image goes to an operator for real-time evaluation. The draft gives no figure for how often.
strings: If the pod can't identify the target and judge it, the draft says an image goes to an operator for real-time evaluation. The draft gives no figure for how often.

S5.headline: About 63 pounds, fully loaded
S5.cite: c12 c13 c14 c30 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S5.body: The draft gives a wingspan of about 7.8 feet, a length of about 8 feet and a maximum payload of 8 pounds. It calls the aircraft highly automated.
strings: The draft gives a wingspan of about 7.8 feet, a length of about 8 feet and a maximum payload of 8 pounds. It calls the aircraft highly automated.
c12 c13 c14 c30 TEXAS AI DOCKET

S6.kicker: The draft's maximum, not flights flown
S6.headline: Up to 220 Chargers
S6.cite: c7 c24 c34 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S6.body: Across Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio the draft caps the proposal at 4,400 Dropboxes and 220,000 deliveries a day. Each mast stands for one Charger, which the draft says would typically be 36 docks in three towers of twelve.
strings: Across Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio the draft caps the proposal at 4,400 Dropboxes and 220,000 deliveries a day. Each mast stands for one Charger, which the draft says would typically be 36 docks in three towers of twelve.

S7.headline: It finds no significant impact
S7.cite: c21 c26 c29 c35 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S7.body: The draft ties 400 deliveries a day to places like a large apartment complex. At that rate it estimates delivery noise at no more than DNL 58.1 dB at any distance from a delivery point. It calls 59.7 dB the line below which a rise of 1.5 dB or more can't be significant.
strings: The draft ties 400 deliveries a day to places like a large apartment complex. At that rate it estimates delivery noise at no more than DNL 58.1 dB at any distance from a delivery point. It calls 59.7 dB the line below which a rise of 1.5 dB or more can't be significant.

S8.headline: Zipline prepared it
S8.cite: c6 c7 c27 c36 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S8.body: The draft says Zipline prepared it under FAA supervision. Its noise figures rest on testing Zipline collected, in a report ICF prepared for the FAA. The page sets passages from across the draft side by side.
strings: The draft says Zipline prepared it under FAA supervision. Its noise figures rest on testing Zipline collected, in a report ICF prepared for the FAA. The page sets passages from across the draft side by side.

S9.headline: Comments close October 11th
S9.cite: c2 c3 c18 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S9.body: The draft gives no figure for how often an operator is sent an image. Email 9-FAA-Drone-Environmental@faa.gov and name the Zipline Texas Draft EA in the subject line.
